_doc: Terminal Chart grade (D-022): the canonical layer-override definition applied to the OpenFreeMap Liberty base style, per theme. Rules run in order; the FIRST rule whose `match` hits a layer applies its paint/layout and stops. `match.type` = MapLibre layer type; `match.idIncludes` = substring test on layer id (any of). Values are resolved from packages/tokens/src/primitives.json — keep them in sync by hand (this file is consumed by native apps at runtime, no build step). Both surfaces (app 8B, portal post-8B) consume this; snapshot-style.mjs bakes it into full committed style JSONs when run with network access.
_revision: 2026-08-08 discovery-layer revision (founder): the chart is a discovery layer, not the product. The prior grade left Liberty's own defaults showing through on every layer it did not name — `landuse_residential` (hsla(0,3%,85%,.84) up to z12) was the bright grey landmass, `boundary_2/3` the prominent dashed lines, `highway-shield-*` the white E1/F265/A1 boxes, `waterway_river` the blue lines, and every symbol shared one flat ink-300 so a village read as loudly as a city. Rules below name every Liberty layer group by its real id (list them with `curl <styleUrl> | jq '.layers[].id'`), give roads and place labels a hierarchy, and ramp street names in only once the user has zoomed into a neighbourhood. ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: `waterway` must precede the road rule (`waterway_tunnel` contains 'tunnel'), the water-name rule must precede the POI rule (`water_name_POInt_label` contains 'poi' — the old grade hid it by accident), major roads must precede the general road rule, and every symbol rule must precede the catch-all. Verified by replaying these rules over all 111 live Liberty layers: zero fall through.

rules._: paper-tinted land (paper-50)
world-zoom relief raster held right down (only drawn below z7)
desaturated chart water
rivers/canals join the water body — before the road rule (waterway_tunnel)
all landcover flattened toward paper-100 — residential/greenspace/sand/aeroway/buildings
extruded buildings flatten into the landcover they sit on
park outlines and runway/taxiway linework vanish into the land
water names present but quiet — BEFORE the POI rule ('poi' ⊂ 'water_name_point_label')
POI + airport noise off — pins are the content
route shields and one-way arrows off — motorway furniture, not marketplace data
street names fade in only at neighbourhood zoom
the geographic anchors stay legible (country/state/city)
towns/villages one step quieter than the anchors
administrative boundaries survive as faint structure, never an outline
major roads carry the structure — before the general road rule
minor roads recede into paper
anything else that speaks
